top.title: Lumumba identifies what’s fueling xenophobia
top.description: •Says Africa cannot fight poverty by turning against fellow Africans Professor Patrick Loch Otieno (PLO) Lumumba has warned that Africa’s failure to create sufficient economic opportunities is fuelling xenophobia. He urged governments to address unemployment, poverty and weak industrial development rather than blame migrants for the continent’s challenges. Lumumba, a renowned Kenyan legal scholar and public speaker, said xenophobia often thrived in societies experiencing economic hardship, where unemployment, inequality and pressure on public services encouraged citizens to regard foreigners as competitors. He spoke as the keynote speaker at the Bridge Club’s grand end-of-year event in Lagos on Thursday. In his address, titled Africa Must Not Become Foreign to Itself: Xenophobia, Pan-Africanism and the Future of African Belonging, Lumumba argued that migrants were frequently made scapegoats for economic problems arising from poor governance and weak institutions. He said: “The foreign trader, worker or entrepreneur can be arrested. The failure to create productive employment over several decades cannot be arrested at a roadblock.” According to him, African governments must look beyond the presence of migrants and examine the structural weaknesses responsible for unemployment, poverty and economic competition. He said the inability of many African countries to industrialise and create productive jobs had forced millions of young people into informal economic activities, where competition for limited opportunities could generate resentment. Lumumba observed that Africa’s economic dependence on exporting raw materials while importing finished products had contributed to the loss of employment opportunities to other economies. “We export crude oil and import refined petroleum. We export cocoa and import chocolate. We export minerals and import the machines, batteries and technologies manufactured from them,” he said. He added that the continent was effectively creating employment opportunities elsewhere while its young population continued to struggle for limited opportunities at home. The legal scholar said the appropriate response to the exploitation of migrant workers was to enforce labour laws against employers rather than encourage hostility towards foreigners. According to him, employers who engage undocumented migrants and pay them below lawful wages create resentment among local workers while benefiting from the division. “The appropriate response is not violence against the migrant. It is enforcement of labour law against the employer,” he said. Lumumba also highlighted the contradiction in Africans celebrating the achievements of their compatriots abroad while treating migrants from other African countries with hostility. top.title: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake edges Troy in final seconds for epic Class A football title win
top.description: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake celebrates after beating Troy for the Section 2, Class A title on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, at Colonie High School in Colonie, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) COLONIE - The waning stages of the fourth quarter Friday night for the Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team were looking painfully dire, as the Spartans found themselves down a point against Troy and forced to give the ball back on a punt. In a span of a few minutes, BH-BL senior standout Login Tomlinson made two of the biggest plays of his career - the first with his hand and the second with his foot - to flip things back in favor of his team in the Section 2 Class A Super Bowl. First, Tomlinson forced Troy junior quarterback Kyair Carr to fumble the ball away at the Flying Horses' 23-yard line. Then, BH-BL had just 17 seconds left when it had Tomlinson line up for a 32-yard field goal on third down and without a timeout remaining. The senior - following a timeout by Troy - drilled a go-ahead, line-drive boot down the middle in what ended up being a thrilling 23-21 Super Bowl victory over the Flying Horses at Colonie High School. "I have been dreaming about this since I was a little kid and first starting kicking," said Tomlinson, a four-year varsity player who is headed to Siena University to play lacrosse. "It happened. It came true." "It was really nerve-racking out there," BH-BL junior quarterback Tristan West said. "I believed in him every moment when he went out there to kick." The pulse-pounding triumph secured BH-BL (11-0) the program's 11th Class A sectional title in 20 years, and first since 2021. It also marked the first championship guided by fourth-year coach Kevin DeBonis. The loss denied Troy, playing in its second straight Super Bowl, a 10th title since first winning one in 1993. "This feels amazing. Since we were little kids, this is what we have been working for," West said. Last year, the Flying Horses lost to Niskayuna. Troy senior fullback/defensive Ben Mergil, who produced two touchdown receptions and recovered a fumble by BH-BL, emerged from an emotional postgame gathering to put the defeat into context. "It is hard, but, at the end of the day, it is football," Mergil said. "Anybody that has ever played football knows it will teach life lessons. Sometimes, things just don't shake out for you, but you just have to roll with the punches. I want to thank my coaches, my teammates and God for giving me this opportunity to play for such an amazing school and play my heart out." Both squads left everything they had on the field. top.title: UTSA athletics inducts fourth Hall of Fame class
top.description: From left to right, Jessica Rogers, Ryanne Dupree, Teresa Neighbors, Leonard Byrd, and Tamara Luckeymeyer were inducted as the fourth class in the UTSA Athletics Hall of Fame during a ceremony on Friday at Pedrotti's Ranch in Helotes. (Vashaun Newman/UTSA Athletics) (Vashaun Newman/UTSA Athletics) UTSA inducted three of the San Antonio area's brightest athletics stars into its 2026 Hall of Fame class during a ceremony Friday at Pedrotti's Ranch. East Central's Ryanne DuPree, Judson's Teresa Neighbors and Marshall's Leonard Byrd joined volleyball standout Tamara Luckeymeyer and softball star Jessica Rogers in UTSA's fourth Hall of Fame class. The three track and field standouts from this year's group join a list of UTSA Hall of Fame track athletes that includes Tameka Roberts-Nunez in the inaugural class as well as Starlite Williams and Teddy Williams in 2024. DuPree was a four-time All-American in the multi-events from 2004 to 2007, finishing as high as fourth in the nation and winning nine conference championships. She also holds four UTSA records, including a mark of 13.23 seconds in the 100-meter hurdles. Neighbors' third-place finish as a senior at the 1990 national championships with a mark of 6.74 seconds in the 55-meter run is tied for the highest women's NCAA Indoor individual finish in program history, setting a UTSA record that still stands. She also set then-school records in the 100 and 2000 in 1989, earning another All-America nod. Byrd was a three-time All-American in the 400-meter sprint during his time at UTSA from 1994 to 1997, finishing as high as third in the 1996 outdoor championships. He won four consecutive Southland outdoor conference titles in the event, claiming eight conference championships overall. Luckemeyer won Southland Conference Player of the Year twice in a career that spanned 1997 to 2000, helping the Roadrunners to a regular-season title in 1999 and a tournament championship in 2000. She holds the school records for kills in a career (2,034) and season (567 in 1999). Rogers was a first-team All-Southland selection in each of her four seasons from 2003 to 2007, winning the league's Player of the Year and Hitter of the Year honors in 2005. She stands as the school's career record holder for runs (159), hits (281), extra-base hits (104) and at-bats (732), and in 2005 she led the nation with 0.38 home runs per game. UTSA's Hall of Fame selection committee is made up of designees from the UTSA Alumni Association Board, Letterwinners Club, Roadrunner Foundation and Student-Athlete Advisory Committee, as well as representatives from the university and athletics department along with local print and electronic media. top.title: 2027: Violence threatens turnout as party supporters come under attacks
top.description: •60 to 70 per cent of voters afraid of voting – security analyst •INEC warns of N10m fine, jail term for inflammatory campaigns •Attacks on rallies, convoys heighten fears By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Between 60 to 70 per cent of Nigerian voters are afraid that political violence will stop them from voting in 2027, a security expert, Mr Onyekachi Adekoya, has said, as voter apathy continues to rise. Adekoya spoke on Friday morning on The Morning Brief, a programme on Channels Television. He cited a calculation by Yiaga Africa. “If you look at Yiaga Africa’s calculation, 60 to 70% of voters are worried that political violence will not allow them come out on the day,” he said. He said that fear works against turnout. “Once the violence and the rhetoric of it goes up, people are less likely to come out to vote, and perhaps that is, some would argue, part of the strategy at play by some parties,” he said. There have been recent incidents, including attacks on party convoys and on an assembly in some states including Delta, Cross River, Lagos, Edo and Gombe states. In Delta State, a man was apprehended and not handed over to the police. He was then reportedly killed. Adekoya said violence was already rising and would get worse. “It is already ticking over 70 incidents captured so far,” he said. “This is not the peak of it because the campaign season has just started.” He said the stakes went beyond 2027, with politicians positioning for 2031 and 2039. “We expect that this political season will be a bit more violent and true to type,” he said. He said pressure on local politicians would raise tensions. “Politicians at the local level are under significant pressure to deliver on their areas and that would most likely raise tensions. What it will look like is that politicians use violence to destabilize the opponents in opponents’ area of strength so that they can lose votes.” Adekoya said his firm’s report classed 14 states as toss-up states, which would be “keenly contested”. He named the North Central, North East and North West, and parts of the South East, as areas of concern. “Nobody should die because somebody is trying to be president,” he said. On what security agencies could do, Adekoya said the shortfall lay in resources. “If at all there is a failure in security it is because of lack of capacity, poor logistics planning and the fact that we have a hydraheaded security problem which cannot be resolved,” he said. He said enforcement could not be left to the agencies alone. “There is a command structure where also politics get in the way of enforcement. It should not be a job only for the police, it should be a collective responsibility,” he said. The concerns followed a run of threats by office holders in several states in recent weeks, which has drawn condemnation from civil society groups, rights organisations and opposition politicians. top.title: Sacking of Atiku: What Justice Lifu based his judgement on
top.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The leadership crisis rocking the African Democratic Congress (ADC) took a decisive turn when Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, invalidated the emergence of Senator David Mark and other executives who assumed control of the party in July 2025. But the judgment of November 5, 2026, was not simply about competing claims to party leadership. It hinged on a fundamental legal question: could the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC) use its constitutional powers to replace an existing elected leadership structure without complying with the democratic procedures prescribed by law? In the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment obtained by Saturday Vanguard, Justice Lifu said he identified critical weaknesses in the defendants’ case, including the disputed resignation letter on which they relied, the limits of NEC’s administrative powers and the absence of satisfactory evidence that the new executives emerged through a democratic election. The resignation letter One of the Mark-led camp’s principal arguments was that Nafiu Bala Gombe had voluntarily resigned as Deputy National Chairman on May 17, 2025, before the NEC meeting that produced the new leadership. The letter, tendered as Exhibit ADC 1, was intended to establish that Gombe had relinquished his position and consequently lacked the legal standing to challenge the subsequent leadership transition. Justice Lifu, however, was unconvinced Rather than accept the document simply because it was certified, the judge examined its signature against Gombe’s signatures on other documents executed before a Commissioner for Oaths. He explained that certification established the status of a document as a true copy but did not, in itself, establish the authenticity of a disputed signature. After comparing the documents, he said that he found material differences in their structure, style, formation and general manner of execution. “The signatures do not appear to be one and the same,” Justice Lifu observed. He consequently described the purported resignation letter as fictitious or fabricated and rejected it as reliable evidence that Gombe had voluntarily vacated his office. The finding removed a central pillar of the defendants’ argument that Gombe had ceased to be an officer of the party before the July 2025 transition. Importantly, this was a finding made in determining the civil dispute, not a criminal conviction for forgery. NEC’s powers could not override the law The second major issue concerned the extent of NEC’s authority under Article 19(14) of the ADC constitution. top.title: South Africa releases Fani-Kayode’s speech after protest
top.description: South Africa’s presidency has released a separate video of Nigeria’s High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, delivering his address at a credentials presentation ceremony, hours after the diplomat protested its omission from the official livestream. Fani-Kayode had raised concerns after the live broadcast of Friday’s ceremony, at which he presented his letters of credence alongside 14 other ambassadors to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, failed to capture his speech. The ceremony took place at the Sefako M. Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Tshwane, Gauteng, and was streamed on the South African presidency’s YouTube channel. The broadcast appeared to experience a technical interruption while French Ambassador to South Africa, Antoine Michon, was speaking. Fani-Kayode was scheduled to speak next, but the livestream cut to Ramaphosa’s address to the assembled diplomats. Reacting to the omission, Fani-Kayode suggested that his exclusion might have been deliberate, alleging that some elements in South Africa did not want to hear his views or see him. “Clearly some elements in South Africa do not want to hear what we have to say or see our faces, but we are here to stay as long as we are welcome and have the confidence of President Ramaphosa, which I am sure we do,” he said. He disclosed that he personally brought the matter to Ramaphosa’s attention during the photo session following the ceremony. According to the Nigerian envoy, the South African president took him to the relevant officials and acted promptly to address his complaint. Hours later, the presidency published a separate recording of Fani-Kayode’s speech on its YouTube channel. In the address, the Nigerian diplomat pledged to strengthen bilateral relations, particularly economic and diplomatic cooperation, between both countries. “Nothing can come between the two of us. And part of my job here is to reset that relationship, to come and build that bridge, and to ensure that whatever concerns we have mutually, we can work them out and move forward together,” he said. Recalling Nigeria’s support for South Africa during the anti-apartheid struggle, Fani-Kayode said the historical ties between both countries provided a strong foundation for closer cooperation. He described Nigeria as South Africa’s largest trading partner in Africa and stressed the importance of sustained collaboration between the two countries in advancing the continent’s interests. “Without South Africa and Nigeria working together, closely together, the destiny of our great continent may well be affected,” he said. Fani-Kayode also commended South Africa’s positions on international issues, including the conflict in Gaza, its participation in the BRICS bloc and its advocacy for the interests of the Global South. He praised Ramaphosa’s efforts towards securing Nigeria’s inclusion in the Group of 20 (G20), describing them as noteworthy and encouraging. The other sat on the goal line fighting back tears in near freezing temperatures. Hurley did push across one talking point during the brief time in front of his team. This season was a success by all measures. One result in November won't diminish it. A perfect season came to a close behind early mistakes and missed opportunities. Give them one more possession in the second half, and the Tigers (12-1) are potentially playing for a spot in Lucas Oil Stadium. They just came up short. Such is football. top.title: Naugatuck football rallies past Torrington as Qwentarvous Lee delivers two huge plays
top.description: Naugatuck's Qwentarvous Lee rushed for 133 yards, while scoring on a 78-yard fumble return and an 80-yard run in a 29-14 win over Torrington on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, at Torrington High. (Steve Barlow/For Hearst Connecticut Media) TORRINGTON - With the annual Thanksgiving battle with Ansonia within sniffing distance, Naugatuck football coach Chris Anderson preached to his team all week long that the Greyhounds couldn't look past Torrington on Friday night. He was right. Naugy found itself trailing by a touchdown at the Robert Frost Athletic Complex, and the gap could have been even greater after another score was called back because of a false start by the Raiders. "At halftime, we told the kids, ‘Well, you've dug yourself a hole, but you've been resilient all season.' We were down to Holy Cross and Woodland, too, and won those games. We can do it again," Anderson remarked following a 29-14 victory that improved the Greyhounds to 9-0. Torrington (6-3) controlled the first half with its ball-control single-wing offense. The Raiders ran 39 plays from scrimmage, more than twice as many as Naugatuck's 17, and ate up big chunks of the clock. Torrington even held the Greyhounds scoreless in the first half for the first time all season. "Yes, we're high-powered, but when you don't have the ball, it doesn't matter," Anderson said. "When you're able to eat the clock like they can, they have the formula to beat us." Naugy, which beat Torrington on the final play each of the past two meetings, needed a big play to turn the tide. Qwentarvous Lee provided exactly that and then did it again. Ahead 8-0 after the opening half, Torrington was driving again on its first possession after intermission. But fullback Cameron Roxbury fumbled at the 22. The ball spun out of the pile to Lee, who picked it up and raced 78 yards to a touchdown. Brandon Andoh's conversion run tied the game for Naugy. "Coach put me in on defense in the second half. I noticed we weren't getting to the ball. I was driving to the ball, and all the effort paid off. The ball came out right in front of me. Josiah (Loyd) stripped it out. The ball came right to me and I took off," Lee said. Nick Coleman got the momentum right back for Torrington with a 61-yard scoring run for his second TD, but Lee immediately answered. On Naugy's next play, he burst through the line and bolted 80 yards for a touchdown. Gabriel Bello's point-after kick put his team ahead for good. "I got Llir (Mamudov) and (Logan) Washenko, two 300-pound guys, in front of me. I told them if you make your blocks and Josiah goes through and blocks the linebacker, I'm going to take off, and that's what happened," Lee said. Torrington answered by driving to the Naugy 6-yard line, but Coleman was stopped short on fourth down. "We just have to keep swarming to the ball. That was the big emphasis for the game," Loyd said. "It means a lot to get to 9-0, especially against a good team like this. They're coached well and have good athletes."

top.title: Cold weather can't cool off Purdue soccer on way to Big Ten Tournament title
top.description: WEST LAFAYETTE — It was a frigid 37 degrees on a day bogged down by rain and sleet, but adrenaline won out against the weather conditions. Purdue soccer 's Jaiden Anderson just added to her program record with her 20th goal, this one delivering a Big Ten Tournament championship in thrilling fashion. Anderson, ignoring the looming Indiana winter weather, ripped off her No. 54 jersey and ran across Folk Field twirling it above her head, was chased down from behind by teammate Emilia Deppe, who tackled Anderson to the ground as the rest of the Boilers dogpiled on top. The Big Ten's Forward of the Year had been marked by two, and sometimes three, Michigan State defenders all night before getting into the open field, juking two Spartans and ripping a shot into the lower right 90 6:35 into overtime to give Purdue a 4-3 victory. "It was just spur of the moment, pure excitement, pure love and passion for this game," Anderson said. It was the latest in a series of thrillers that brought the Boilermakers their first Big Ten Tournament championship since 2007 and the second victory this season over third-ranked Michigan State. Purdue earned its first NCAA Tournament appearance since 2021 , doing so a season after not even qualifying for the Big Ten's eight-team postseason tournament. top.description: ‘Don’t Act Soft Now,’ ‘You’re Gonna Get Smoked’ — NFL Fans React to Titans HC Robert Saleh Downplaying Beef With Jaguars HC Liam Coen The rivalry between Robert Saleh and Liam Coen is back in the spotlight ahead of the Week 10 showdown between the Tennessee Titans and the Jacksonville Jaguars. The two traded heated words on the field last season, but Saleh now sounds ready to bury the hatchet. He recently had kind words for Coen and the Jaguars’ coaching staff, a turn that caught NFL fans flat-footed. Fans React to Robert Saleh Squashing Beef With Liam Coen The tension between the two coaches dates back to September 2025, when Saleh was the San Francisco 49ers’ defensive coordinator. He made headlines after praising Jacksonville’s offensive preparation, describing Coen’s staff as having “legally, a really advanced signal-stealing-type system.” Coen apparently took the comment as an accusation and confronted Saleh after the Jaguars defeated the 49ers 26-21. The two coaches exchanged heated words at midfield and had to be separated. Coen was reportedly heard telling Saleh, “Keep my name out of your mouth.” What looked like the start of a bitter coaching rivalry, however, didn’t last long. Both men later said they had cleared the air at the NFL’s annual league meetings in Phoenix in March. Saleh’s comments on Friday suggest the hatchet is still buried. “Liam’s great, man,” the Titans head coach said. “We’ve had plenty of interactions. top.description: LAS VEGAS, NV - NOVEMBER 11: Rollie Fingers greets William Contreras during the 2026 MLB Awards presented by MGM Rewards at The Chelsea at The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas on Wednesday, November 11, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Matt Aguirre/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images This week, the GM Meetings took place in Las Vegas. It is the first real chance for GMs to meet and discuss trade possibilities with other teams, as well as hold initial meetings with free agents. It was also awards week for MLB, with the yearly awards all announced. Here’s what took place this week. There wasn’t much for free agent deals, but a few were signed this week to kick off free agency. The big news for the Brewers was Jake Bauers signing with the Red Sox , which also means that he turned down the qualifying offer from Milwaukee. Bauers signed a four year, $58 million contract with the Red Sox, and the Brewers will receive a compensatory draft pick after the first round. A couple of other free agents were signed at the meetings, with Emilio Pagan signing with the Tigers and Evan Phillips signing with the Braves. Another piece of news for the Brewers was about Jeferson Quero. The Brewers were officially granted a fourth option year for Quero , meaning they can keep him in the minors for one more year. Without the option, Quero would either have to make the roster out of spring training or potentially be exposed to waivers to keep in the minors. Now, the Brewers can give him one more season in Nashville to see what he can offer in the future. Early trade rumors are coming up for current Brewers’ players, mainly focused around the players who are free agents after the 2027 season. The main two players that have been mentioned in rumors so far are Trevor Megill and William Contreras. At the meetings, Matt Arnold spoke about the possibility of trading Contreras . He did it with usual GM speak, saying that Contreras “means a lot to this team”. When asked about Megill, he continued with the GM speak and said, “He got the last six outs of the World Series, and I just went to a Metallica concert with him, so I like him. I like him a lot.” The yearly awards were also announced at this year’s meetings, and as expected for the World Series champions, they were represented several times. Here is a summary of the awards that they won or received votes for: Logan Henderson finished sixth in the NL Rookie of the Year vote, with Sal Stewart of the Reds and Kevin McGonigle of the Tigers taking the award . Manager Pat Murphy won his third straight NL Manager of the Year award , while Will Venable of the White Sox won it in the AL. Jacob Misiorowski was a unanimous winner of the NL Cy Young award , with Cam Schlitter also a unanimous winner in the AL. Trevor Megill finished third in the inaugural Reliever of the Year award, with Mason Miller taking the award in the NL and Louis Varland in the AL. Aaron Ashby and Abner Uribe also received votes. top.title: Canada embrace Concacaf experience in win over Guatemala
top.description: Canada embrace Concacaf experience in win over Guatemala By Ben Steiner A fireworks-filled anthem, a less-than-ideal playing surface, and cages surrounding the pitch. Away days in Concacaf aren’t for the faint of heart, but Canada scraped out a 3-2 win over Guatemala on Friday. Under head coach Jesse Marsch, Canada have faced some of the world's best teams and reached the FIFA World Cup Round of 16. Yet Friday's opening 45 minutes of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals may have been among their most complete, before a disheartening second half saw a 3-0 lead nearly disappear. Jonathan David brought his stellar LaLiga form to the Estadio El Trébol, posting 1g/1a and helping build up Canada’s third goal. Liam Millar, in dominant form in the EFL Championship, scored too, while former Minnesota United striker Tani Oluwaseyi netted his first for Canada in 18 appearances. “We were very happy with that start,” assistant coach Mauro Biello told reporters, taking media duties after Marsch’s second-half red card. “It was something that we addressed here in the build-up to be able to create more, to score more goals, and I think we're very happy with the way our forwards played. Especially in the first half, and getting goals from both strikers and Liam, who was also doing really well at his club.” Alphonso Davies blow It had been more than 600 days since Alphonso Davies last started for Canada, when he tore his ACL in the 2025 Nations League third-place game against the United States . It seemed as if his return, committing to playing for Les Rouges on a November night in Guatemala amid stellar FC Bayern Munich form, was him putting the last two years of injury troubles behind him. That hope lasted just five minutes before an awkward shot block sent him off the pitch early. As of Friday, it was unclear if Davies would be available for the pivotal second leg in Canada or fly back to Germany to recover. top.description: FBL-FRIENDLY-ARG-URU - AFP Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni has called for patience with his emerging youngsters after the Albiceleste suffered a 2-1 friendly defeat against Uruguay at La Bombonera on Friday. Playing their first match since Lionel Messi retired from international football last month, the hosts could not overturn two quickfire second-half goals in Buenos Aires. We knew it would be tough, and now we just have to keep working." Protecting his youngsters, he added: "We couldn't quite find the right moments for the young lads to play their natural game. We can't expect them to carry the team on their shoulders - it's tough, and their team-mates will help them through it. As for the fans, they'll come back to cheer us on, even though he's no longer here. It's up to us to spark that enthusiasm in the supporters." He explained: "You never plan to lose... Duke controlled the boards early though, and got off to an early, if slow lead, at 6-2. Then the team just took off, going on a 25-6 run, behind a pair of threes from Caleb Foster, and an 11-0 burst, en route to a 90-47 win. SIUE fouled a lot early, putting Duke in the bonus in the first five minutes. nigeria.title: Lumumba identifies what’s fueling xenophobia
nigeria.description: •Says Africa cannot fight poverty by turning against fellow Africans Professor Patrick Loch Otieno (PLO) Lumumba has warned that Africa’s failure to create sufficient economic opportunities is fuelling xenophobia. He urged governments to address unemployment, poverty and weak industrial development rather than blame migrants for the continent’s challenges. Lumumba, a renowned Kenyan legal scholar and public speaker, said xenophobia often thrived in societies experiencing economic hardship, where unemployment, inequality and pressure on public services encouraged citizens to regard foreigners as competitors. He spoke as the keynote speaker at the Bridge Club’s grand end-of-year event in Lagos on Thursday. In his address, titled Africa Must Not Become Foreign to Itself: Xenophobia, Pan-Africanism and the Future of African Belonging, Lumumba argued that migrants were frequently made scapegoats for economic problems arising from poor governance and weak institutions. He said: “The foreign trader, worker or entrepreneur can be arrested. The failure to create productive employment over several decades cannot be arrested at a roadblock.” According to him, African governments must look beyond the presence of migrants and examine the structural weaknesses responsible for unemployment, poverty and economic competition. He said the inability of many African countries to industrialise and create productive jobs had forced millions of young people into informal economic activities, where competition for limited opportunities could generate resentment. Lumumba observed that Africa’s economic dependence on exporting raw materials while importing finished products had contributed to the loss of employment opportunities to other economies. “We export crude oil and import refined petroleum. We export cocoa and import chocolate. We export minerals and import the machines, batteries and technologies manufactured from them,” he said. He added that the continent was effectively creating employment opportunities elsewhere while its young population continued to struggle for limited opportunities at home. The legal scholar said the appropriate response to the exploitation of migrant workers was to enforce labour laws against employers rather than encourage hostility towards foreigners. According to him, employers who engage undocumented migrants and pay them below lawful wages create resentment among local workers while benefiting from the division. “The appropriate response is not violence against the migrant. It is enforcement of labour law against the employer,” he said. Lumumba also highlighted the contradiction in Africans celebrating the achievements of their compatriots abroad while treating migrants from other African countries with hostility. Adekoya spoke on Friday morning on The Morning Brief, a programme on Channels Television. He cited a calculation by Yiaga Africa. “If you look at Yiaga Africa’s calculation, 60 to 70% of voters are worried that political violence will not allow them come out on the day,” he said. He said that fear works against turnout. “Once the violence and the rhetoric of it goes up, people are less likely to come out to vote, and perhaps that is, some would argue, part of the strategy at play by some parties,” he said. There have been recent incidents, including attacks on party convoys and on an assembly in some states including Delta, Cross River, Lagos, Edo and Gombe states. In Delta State, a man was apprehended and not handed over to the police. He was then reportedly killed. But the judgment of November 5, 2026, was not simply about competing claims to party leadership. It hinged on a fundamental legal question: could the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC) use its constitutional powers to replace an existing elected leadership structure without complying with the democratic procedures prescribed by law? In the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment obtained by Saturday Vanguard, Justice Lifu said he identified critical weaknesses in the defendants’ case, including the disputed resignation letter on which they relied, the limits of NEC’s administrative powers and the absence of satisfactory evidence that the new executives emerged through a democratic election. The resignation letter One of the Mark-led camp’s principal arguments was that Nafiu Bala Gombe had voluntarily resigned as Deputy National Chairman on May 17, 2025, before the NEC meeting that produced the new leadership. The letter, tendered as Exhibit ADC 1, was intended to establish that Gombe had relinquished his position and consequently lacked the legal standing to challenge the subsequent leadership transition. Justice Lifu, however, was unconvinced Rather than accept the document simply because it was certified, the judge examined its signature against Gombe’s signatures on other documents executed before a Commissioner for Oaths. He explained that certification established the status of a document as a true copy but did not, in itself, establish the authenticity of a disputed signature. After comparing the documents, he said that he found material differences in their structure, style, formation and general manner of execution. “The signatures do not appear to be one and the same,” Justice Lifu observed. He consequently described the purported resignation letter as fictitious or fabricated and rejected it as reliable evidence that Gombe had voluntarily vacated his office. The finding removed a central pillar of the defendants’ argument that Gombe had ceased to be an officer of the party before the July 2025 transition. Importantly, this was a finding made in determining the civil dispute, not a criminal conviction for forgery. NEC’s powers could not override the law The second major issue concerned the extent of NEC’s authority under Article 19(14) of the ADC constitution. In January 2023, the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop following an outage involving its Notice to Air Missions (NOTAM) system, which provides pilots with critical information about hazards, changes to airport facilities and other developments that could affect flight operations. nigeria.title: World Diabetes Day: High cost pushes drugs, special diets out of reach
nigeria.description: As the world marks the 2026 World Diabetes Day today, attention is once again drawn to the importance of early diagnosis, timely treatment and sustained care in preventing complications and saving lives. But for many Nigerians living with the condition, the challenge goes beyond early detection to affording medication, special diets and regular medical checks needed to manage the disease. Some patients who spoke to Weekend Trust said the rising cost of treatment had pushed them into financial hardship, forcing them to ration prescribed drugs, compromise their diets or go for days without medication. For Mrs Ngunengen Akpam, living with diabetes has become a daily struggle, not only against the disease but also against the rising cost of managing it. Tinubu booed at Abuja mosque after Friday prayers Women and race to 2027 The burden is compounded by her responsibility to also support her diabetic mother, Mama Lydia Acka, making the cost of medication, food and routine medical care a constant source of worry for the family. Akpam told one of our correspondents that the prices of essential diabetes medications had increased considerably over the years, making it increasingly difficult to maintain the treatment prescribed by her doctors. She recalled that Metformin, one of the drugs she takes, which sold for N700 for a pack of three cards in 2015, now costs about N2,500. Similarly, Dormin, which previously sold for N700, now costs N3,500 for a pack of 10 cards, she said. “The cost of drugs has increased tremendously. I take my medication twice daily, so it is not easy. In a month, we spend so much, especially when you have another diabetic person to cater for,” she said. Medication, however, is only part of the financial burden. nigeria.description: I came looking for ancient soldiers and left thinking about Nigeria’s tourism potential. One thing I was particularly looking forward to during my visit to China was seeing the famous Terracotta Warriors in Xi’an. I had read about them, seen pictures, and of course, watched films inspired by the mysteries of ancient China. But nothing quite prepared me for the experience of standing in front of thousands of life-sized soldiers who have been buried underground for more than 2,000 years. And what an experience it was! If you have watched Hollywood’s The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor, you may remember the mysterious army of clay soldiers that comes alive. Well, I finally got to see the real thing. Thankfully, none of them came alive while I was there. But standing in those enormous exhibition halls, surrounded by thousands of soldiers, horses and chariots arranged in military formation, I couldn’t help wondering what must have gone through the minds of the people who created this extraordinary army. The story takes us back to 221 BC when Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor to unify China. Like many powerful rulers of his time, he was obsessed with immortality and the idea of continuing his reign beyond death. His solution was to build an entire underground army to protect him in the afterlife. Think about that. While some people prepared for retirement, this emperor was preparing for eternity, complete with his own military formation. The scale of the project is difficult to comprehend. Thousands of life-sized clay soldiers, horses and chariots were painstakingly created. Above the excavation pit in Xi’an, I stood where visitors have looked down on the Terracotta Army for decades: thousands of figures, each made by hand, and still not fully unearthed. What makes the discovery even more fascinating is that the soldiers are not identical. They have different facial features, hairstyles, uniforms and expressions. They look like real individuals, each with a distinct identity and military rank. Then comes another remarkable twist. For over 2,000 years, this enormous army remained hidden beneath the earth until 1974 when some local farmers digging a well stumbled upon fragments of what would become one of the greatest archaeological discoveries in modern history. Imagine going out to dig a well and discovering an entire army. I wonder what the conversation was like that evening when they returned home. Today, the site is recognised globally as one of the greatest archaeological treasures in the world, and is popularly described as the Eighth Wonder of the World. The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) designated the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor a World Heritage Site in 1987. nigeria.description: On Saturday, November 7, Nigeria’s Flamingos edged out Asian giants Japan 2-1 in Rabat, Morocco, to lift the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. They became the first African nation to claim the global title and placed Nigeria alongside France as the only countries to win both the men’s and women’s U-17 World Cups. The Flamingos’ male counterparts, the Golden Eaglets—with five titles—remain the most successful team in the world at that level. The victorious Flamingos returned to Nigeria on Monday, November 9, to a rousing welcome. Yet amid the national celebrations, federal cash rewards, and Senate commendations, a familiar anxiety lingers over the future of the young players. For decades, Nigeria has dominated youth tournaments, only to watch many of its brightest teenage sensations fade into obscurity. While stars like Victor Osimhen and Asisat Oshoala successfully transitioned to the global stage, countless others, hampered by poor management, unhealed injuries, or structural neglect, abandoned football altogether before their prime. Indeed, the history of Nigerian football is replete with stories of teenage sensations who sparkled at dawn with youth national teams only to fade into obscurity before noon. Thus, in spite of Nigeria’s dominance at the U-17 level, the country is yet to taste global victory at the U-20 level. The Flying Eagles, the team meant to harness the best talent from victorious U-17 squads, have managed to claim only two silver medals and one bronze since their first appearance in 1983. Similarly, only a handful of players have successfully transitioned from the U-17 to the U-20 and senior Super Eagles squads. Nduka Ugbade, Jonathan Akpoborie, Celestine Babayaro, Mikel Obi, Chinedu Obasi, Lukman Haruna, Ramon Azeez, Isaac Success and Taiwo Awoniyi are among the few who completed the full international pathway. One of the biggest leaks in Nigerian football happens immediately after a youth tournament ends. Without a centralised database, young players return to disorganised local setups and vanish from national team radars. It is, therefore, a step in the right direction that the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has promised to preserve the core of the victorious Flamingos, with 11 players still eligible for the next U-17 competition. Many of us, including your correspondent, then based in Kaduna, were particularly enchanted by his one-hour Sunday evening television broadcasts on Channels Television where he blended Old Testament religious proclamations with contemporary political discourse in a manner that was both captivating and intellectually engaging. He was in the mould of Elijah, who challenged the wicked King Ahab; John the Baptist, who confronted Herod; and Jesus Christ, who fearlessly challenged the religious establishment and the political order represented by the likes of Herod, whom He described as a fox. Bakare projected the image of a preacher who was not afraid to speak truth to power, whether in the church or in government. His interventions were often forceful, his biblical references uncompromising, and his denunciations of religious excesses particularly refreshing to many who believed that the pulpit should remain a place of truth and accountability. The questions about Bakare, however, began to emerge after he joined the political fray. His association with Muhammadu Buhari during the 2011 election cycle was his first major public adventure into partisan politics. The political partnership did not produce the expected electoral outcome. Some questioned his movement from the pulpit to the political podium, particularly against the backdrop of scriptural cautions about the tension between spiritual devotion and the worldly considerations that often drive political contests. His less-than-expected reaction to the killings of mostly Christian National Youth Service Corps members in the aftermath of the 2011 election would also have disappointed many who had looked up to him as a moral voice. Yet, his political journey continued. Before the 2023 presidential election, Bakare made an even more remarkable declaration: that he would become Nigeria’s 16th president. Many, including yours sincerely, took the pronouncement seriously, largely because of the regard in which he was held as a servant of God. A preacher who speaks with such certainty about the future, particularly when presenting it as a divine revelation, invites people to believe that his words are informed by something beyond personal ambition. The outcome of the APC presidential primary in June 2022 was therefore particularly instructive. Pastor Bakare scored zero votes. nigeria.description: The harm Nigerian importers have done to the Chinese brand is incalculable. For years, we had been led to believe that Chinese products were inferior. Even now, despite empirical evidence to the contrary, I still hesitate to buy Chinese spare parts whether they are for my car or house. That is how deep the ‘brainwashing’ has gone. And it is not without reason. Several Chinese goods which were branded as cheaper had disappointed in the past. But the same Chinese goods were making in-roads into European and American markets with relative ease. These are countries that are historically fussy about standards for imported goods. How can a country that has become so industrialized that it is giving the almighty US sleepless nights be so negatively branded in Nigeria? The mystery was confounding. Yet the answer turned out to be relatively simple. Nigerian importers, AKA as ‘businessmen’ went and combed the hinterland in China to deliberately access or request for inferior goods, and sometimes scraps, for greater profit. In other words, Nigerians made Nigeria a dumping ground. And the regulating authorities were complicit to say the least because these goods pass through our borders and ports. This was the same thing they reportedly did with pharmaceutical products from India as that Asian country was emerging as the pharmaceutical capital of the world with its cheaper, generic versions of branded drugs. Things got so bad that many popular antibiotic brands had either been faked or their potency significantly reduced. The result was that drugs that were supposed to heal caused deaths. Inexplicable and sometimes painful deaths. Doctors started prescribing less common but probably more expensive alternatives just to protect the lives of their patients. Nothing I have stated here is unknown to the average Nigerian, let alone the relevant authorities. These fake goods and drugs must have come in shiploads to have made the kind of impact they had made. Yet, where are the authorities? Where is intelligence? Our official borders, with their several layers of government agents, are probably among the most manned in the world. They are adept at straining gnats while allowing camels a safe passage. entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Nigerian streaming platform KAVA is set to bring the psychological thriller series Spiraling , starring Toni Tones ( King of Boys ) and Jim Iyke , to audiences across its streaming service. Set against the high-stakes worlds of technology, power and politics in contemporary Nigeria, Spiraling follows Sade ( Toni Tones ), a brilliant tech entrepreneur whose carefully constructed life begins to unravel after an impulsive affair triggers a dangerous chain of events. Spiraling explores the darker side of ambition and the lengths people will go to protect their carefully constructed lives. Alongside Tones and Iyke, the ensemble cast includes Folu Storms , Seun Ajayi , Fae Olumide , Fiyinfoluwa Asenuga and Mathilda Akatugba . Created and directed by Wande Thomas ( Under the Influence , The Smart Money Woman ), the series is co-written by Thomas and Amaka Anioji and produced by Isoken Ogiemwonyi ( The Smart Money Woman , Ci ) . Director and creator Wande Thomas added: I wanted to explore how quickly an ordinary decision can spiral into something completely beyond your control. At its heart, this is a story about the secrets we keep, the lies we tell ourselves and how far we’ll go when everything is at stake. I’m excited for audiences to finally experience it. F Taofeeq/Spiraling Producer Isoken Ogiemwonyi said: With Spiraling , we wanted to take a simple story and tell it really well. We spent a lot of time developing the characters and exploring the darker side of very human emotions, ambition, desire and jealousy. At its heart, it’s a character-driven story about flawed people making questionable decisions, and we’re excited to partner with KAVA to bring it to audiences across Africa and the diaspora. Ladun Awobokun , Head of Acquisitions at KAVA commented : Spiraling is exactly the kind of bold, sophisticated African storytelling we want to champion at KAVA. With its compelling performances and distinctly Nigerian setting, the series delivers a gripping thriller that we believe will resonate with audiences at home and around the world. We’re delighted to bring it to our viewers. Spiraling will be available to stream on KAVA on the 26th of November. Follow @spiralingseries for updates. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. entertainment.title: From Talking Drums to Tourism Diplomacy: How Nigeria Captured Attention at WTM London 2026
entertainment.description: With NTDA leading the national delegation, NTT Global Destinations mobilising international partnerships and diaspora networks, and NANTA representing Nigeria’s private tourism sector, the Nigeria Pavilion became a vibrant celebration of culture, community and tourism opportunities. For three exciting days, Nigeria brought its rhythm, culture, hospitality and entrepreneurial spirit to the global stage at World Travel Market (WTM) London 2026, held from 3 to 5 November at ExCeL London. Led by the Nigerian Tourism Development Authority (NTDA), under its Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, the Nigeria Pavilion welcomed international visitors, tourism professionals, Nigerians and Africans living in the United Kingdom, and industry stakeholders who travelled from Nigeria. Supporting the national showcase was NTT Global Destinations (NGD), NTDA’s Strategic and Pavilion Implementation Partner, responsible for coordinating the exhibition’s planning, stakeholder engagement, international liaison and delivery. Together with the National Association of Nigeria Travel Agencies (NANTA) and diaspora media partners, Nigeria created an experience that extended beyond destination marketing. Day One: Nigeria Arrives in Colour and Rhythm The opening day brought the Nigeria Pavilion to life with traditional talking drums, cultural performances, networking and opportunities for visitors to experience Nigeria’s creative identity. From the energetic rhythms to conversations about Nigeria’s tourism offering, the pavilion quickly became a gathering point for visitors interested in discovering more about the country. Among the highlights was the opportunity to connect Nigerian culture with the global appeal of Nollywood, Afrobeats and contemporary African creativity. The Director General Who Stole the Show Perhaps one of the most memorable moments came when NTDA Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, joined the traditional drummers and dancers in an energetic cultural performance. Rather than remaining a spectator, the DG became part of the attraction, embracing the rhythm and excitement of the Nigerian showcase. His performance drew attention and captured the spirit of the exhibition: a country confidently presenting its culture to the world. It was tourism diplomacy in its most authentic form, demonstrating that sometimes the most powerful way to promote a destination is simply to experience and celebrate it. Day Two: Tourism, Tradition and Private Sector Connections The second day combined cultural discovery with industry engagement, featuring a traditional palm wine experience, networking and interactions between Nigerian tourism stakeholders and international visitors. entertainment.title: Olamide’s Time & Space Is Almost Here! See the Cover Art & 10 Track List
entertainment.description: Olamide releases his new single Burukutu alongside his upcoming album Time & Space. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram If Olamide ‘s ‘ Burukutu ‘ has been on repeat, here’s something else to get into: the rapper has revealed the cover art and full tracklist for his upcoming album, Time & Space . Scheduled for release on November 16, 2026, under YBNL Nation and EMPIRE, the ten-track body of work follows a remarkable lineage of musical evolution from one of Africa’s most enduring creative forces. Adding a deeply personal touch to the rollout, Olamide revealed that he personally painted the striking cover art for the project. Olamide hand-painted the official artwork for his upcoming Time & Space, released via YBNL Nation and EMPIRE. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram Listeners have already caught an exciting glimpse of what to expect from the record through the release of the lead single, Burukutu . Named after the traditional, locally brewed fermented grain beverage, the track serves up rich street-level jubilation and celebratory culture, anchored by rhythmic cadences and unmistakable Yoruba-inflected delivery. The musical journey of Time & Space spans ten carefully curated titles designed to showcase his artistic range. The newly revealed tracklist opens with “ Elohim ” as the introductory piece, followed sequentially by “ Skoskola “, “ Say Less “, the lead anthem “ Burukutu “, and “ Alujon ” rounding out the first half. The second half picks up the tempo with “ Mbiri “, the collaborative track “ Jaiye ” featuring vocalist Fola , followed by “ Oshey “, “ Ring “, and the closing record “ Jogor “. Keeping features remarkably streamlined, the album highlights a targeted guest appearance from Nigerian singer Fola, allowing Olamide’s distinctive penmanship and vocal direction to take centre stage across the entire tracklist. Where that previous body of work leaned into massive collaborative constellations, Time & Space scales back into a more intimate, focused exploration of sound, anchored tightly by the creative vision of the YBNL boss himself. As November 16 approaches, anticipation continues to build across Lagos and beyond, cementing yet another brilliant chapter in Olamide’s legendary catalogue. First introduced as Maltona in 1976 and renamed Maltina in 1977, the brand has maintained a strong presence in Nigerian homes for over five decades. Its journey has been defined by a commitment to nourishment, including its introduction of multivitamin enrichment in 1993 and calcium fortification in 2009. The refreshed packaging features an enriched signature orange, gold accents and barley elements that reinforce Maltina’s malt credentials. The updated sunrays represent vitality and optimism, while the more prominent calcium coin highlights its nourishment proposition. The gold crown cork and the addition of ‘Since 1976’ further celebrate the brand’s heritage. entertainment.description: Alex Unusual’s gold grillz, crystal floral choker, and cherub-accented sunglasses. Who says a buba has to be paired with a wrapper? Nigerian actress, media personality, and reality television star Asogwa Alexandra A —popularly known as Alex Unusua l—is giving us another way to wear the traditional Yoruba top, and her look for the premiere of Loving Itohan makes a strong case for pairing it with a mini skirt. The actress chose a bright fuchsia satin buba with wide half-sleeves, styling it with a fitted mini skirt made from emerald-green and magenta floral brocade damask . It’s an interesting way to rethink the familiar iro and bubacombination: keep the traditional top, swap the wrapper for a shorter skirt, and let the difference in fabric and colour give the outfit its character. The smooth finish of the pink satin against the patterned damask also shows how to wear two statement fabrics without making them compete . The trick is to give each piece a clear role, with the pink buba providing a bold block of colour and the brocade bringing in pattern and texture. Alex Unusual puts a modern spin on the Yoruba iro and buba with a satin top and brocade mini skirt. The mini skirt also gives the outfit a contemporary take on the Oleku silhouette, which traditionally pairs a loose or fitted buba with a wrapper tied above the knee. Alex’s version plays with that familiar proportion, using a fitted damask skirt in place of the wrapper. If you are wondering how to wear a buba and mini skirt without the proportions feeling off, the secret is balancing volume with structure. Because a traditional buba comes with a relaxed cut and wide sleeves, tucking it cleanly into a fitted, high-waisted mini skirt defines the waist and keeps the silhouette neat rather than boxy. Mixing textures intentionally helps too—pairing a plain silk, satin, or AsoOke top with a patterned damask, jacquard, or beaded mini skirt lets both pieces complement each other rather than clash. sports.title: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake edges Troy in final seconds for epic Class A football title win
sports.description: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake celebrates after beating Troy for the Section 2, Class A title on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, at Colonie High School in Colonie, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) COLONIE - The waning stages of the fourth quarter Friday night for the Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team were looking painfully dire, as the Spartans found themselves down a point against Troy and forced to give the ball back on a punt. In a span of a few minutes, BH-BL senior standout Login Tomlinson made two of the biggest plays of his career - the first with his hand and the second with his foot - to flip things back in favor of his team in the Section 2 Class A Super Bowl. First, Tomlinson forced Troy junior quarterback Kyair Carr to fumble the ball away at the Flying Horses' 23-yard line. Then, BH-BL had just 17 seconds left when it had Tomlinson line up for a 32-yard field goal on third down and without a timeout remaining. The senior - following a timeout by Troy - drilled a go-ahead, line-drive boot down the middle in what ended up being a thrilling 23-21 Super Bowl victory over the Flying Horses at Colonie High School. "I have been dreaming about this since I was a little kid and first starting kicking," said Tomlinson, a four-year varsity player who is headed to Siena University to play lacrosse. "It happened. It came true." "It was really nerve-racking out there," BH-BL junior quarterback Tristan West said. "I believed in him every moment when he went out there to kick." The pulse-pounding triumph secured BH-BL (11-0) the program's 11th Class A sectional title in 20 years, and first since 2021. It also marked the first championship guided by fourth-year coach Kevin DeBonis. The loss denied Troy, playing in its second straight Super Bowl, a 10th title since first winning one in 1993. "This feels amazing. Since we were little kids, this is what we have been working for," West said. Last year, the Flying Horses lost to Niskayuna. sports.title: UTSA athletics inducts fourth Hall of Fame class
sports.description: From left to right, Jessica Rogers, Ryanne Dupree, Teresa Neighbors, Leonard Byrd, and Tamara Luckeymeyer were inducted as the fourth class in the UTSA Athletics Hall of Fame during a ceremony on Friday at Pedrotti's Ranch in Helotes. (Vashaun Newman/UTSA Athletics) (Vashaun Newman/UTSA Athletics) UTSA inducted three of the San Antonio area's brightest athletics stars into its 2026 Hall of Fame class during a ceremony Friday at Pedrotti's Ranch. East Central's Ryanne DuPree, Judson's Teresa Neighbors and Marshall's Leonard Byrd joined volleyball standout Tamara Luckeymeyer and softball star Jessica Rogers in UTSA's fourth Hall of Fame class. The three track and field standouts from this year's group join a list of UTSA Hall of Fame track athletes that includes Tameka Roberts-Nunez in the inaugural class as well as Starlite Williams and Teddy Williams in 2024. DuPree was a four-time All-American in the multi-events from 2004 to 2007, finishing as high as fourth in the nation and winning nine conference championships. She also holds four UTSA records, including a mark of 13.23 seconds in the 100-meter hurdles. Neighbors' third-place finish as a senior at the 1990 national championships with a mark of 6.74 seconds in the 55-meter run is tied for the highest women's NCAA Indoor individual finish in program history, setting a UTSA record that still stands. She also set then-school records in the 100 and 2000 in 1989, earning another All-America nod. Byrd was a three-time All-American in the 400-meter sprint during his time at UTSA from 1994 to 1997, finishing as high as third in the 1996 outdoor championships. He won four consecutive Southland outdoor conference titles in the event, claiming eight conference championships overall. Luckemeyer won Southland Conference Player of the Year twice in a career that spanned 1997 to 2000, helping the Roadrunners to a regular-season title in 1999 and a tournament championship in 2000. She holds the school records for kills in a career (2,034) and season (567 in 1999). Rogers was a first-team All-Southland selection in each of her four seasons from 2003 to 2007, winning the league's Player of the Year and Hitter of the Year honors in 2005. She stands as the school's career record holder for runs (159), hits (281), extra-base hits (104) and at-bats (732), and in 2005 she led the nation with 0.38 home runs per game. UTSA's Hall of Fame selection committee is made up of designees from the UTSA Alumni Association Board, Letterwinners Club, Roadrunner Foundation and Student-Athlete Advisory Committee, as well as representatives from the university and athletics department along with local print and electronic media. sports.title: Naugatuck football rallies past Torrington as Qwentarvous Lee delivers two huge plays
sports.description: Naugatuck's Qwentarvous Lee rushed for 133 yards, while scoring on a 78-yard fumble return and an 80-yard run in a 29-14 win over Torrington on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, at Torrington High. (Steve Barlow/For Hearst Connecticut Media) TORRINGTON - With the annual Thanksgiving battle with Ansonia within sniffing distance, Naugatuck football coach Chris Anderson preached to his team all week long that the Greyhounds couldn't look past Torrington on Friday night. He was right. Naugy found itself trailing by a touchdown at the Robert Frost Athletic Complex, and the gap could have been even greater after another score was called back because of a false start by the Raiders. "At halftime, we told the kids, ‘Well, you've dug yourself a hole, but you've been resilient all season.' We were down to Holy Cross and Woodland, too, and won those games. We can do it again," Anderson remarked following a 29-14 victory that improved the Greyhounds to 9-0. Torrington (6-3) controlled the first half with its ball-control single-wing offense. The Raiders ran 39 plays from scrimmage, more than twice as many as Naugatuck's 17, and ate up big chunks of the clock. Torrington even held the Greyhounds scoreless in the first half for the first time all season. "Yes, we're high-powered, but when you don't have the ball, it doesn't matter," Anderson said. "When you're able to eat the clock like they can, they have the formula to beat us." Naugy, which beat Torrington on the final play each of the past two meetings, needed a big play to turn the tide. Qwentarvous Lee provided exactly that and then did it again. Ahead 8-0 after the opening half, Torrington was driving again on its first possession after intermission. But fullback Cameron Roxbury fumbled at the 22. The ball spun out of the pile to Lee, who picked it up and raced 78 yards to a touchdown. Brandon Andoh's conversion run tied the game for Naugy. "Coach put me in on defense in the second half. I noticed we weren't getting to the ball. I was driving to the ball, and all the effort paid off. The ball came out right in front of me. Josiah (Loyd) stripped it out. The ball came right to me and I took off," Lee said. Nick Coleman got the momentum right back for Torrington with a 61-yard scoring run for his second TD, but Lee immediately answered. On Naugy's next play, he burst through the line and bolted 80 yards for a touchdown. Gabriel Bello's point-after kick put his team ahead for good. "I got Llir (Mamudov) and (Logan) Washenko, two 300-pound guys, in front of me. I told them if you make your blocks and Josiah goes through and blocks the linebacker, I'm going to take off, and that's what happened," Lee said. Torrington answered by driving to the Naugy 6-yard line, but Coleman was stopped short on fourth down. "We just have to keep swarming to the ball. That was the big emphasis for the game," Loyd said. "It means a lot to get to 9-0, especially against a good team like this. They're coached well and have good athletes."

It was the latest in a series of thrillers that brought the Boilermakers their first Big Ten Tournament championship since 2007 and the second victory this season over third-ranked Michigan State. sports.title: 2026 GM Meetings Recap
sports.description: LAS VEGAS, NV - NOVEMBER 11: Rollie Fingers greets William Contreras during the 2026 MLB Awards presented by MGM Rewards at The Chelsea at The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas on Wednesday, November 11, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Matt Aguirre/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images This week, the GM Meetings took place in Las Vegas. It is the first real chance for GMs to meet and discuss trade possibilities with other teams, as well as hold initial meetings with free agents. It was also awards week for MLB, with the yearly awards all announced. Here’s what took place this week. There wasn’t much for free agent deals, but a few were signed this week to kick off free agency. The big news for the Brewers was Jake Bauers signing with the Red Sox , which also means that he turned down the qualifying offer from Milwaukee. Bauers signed a four year, $58 million contract with the Red Sox, and the Brewers will receive a compensatory draft pick after the first round. A couple of other free agents were signed at the meetings, with Emilio Pagan signing with the Tigers and Evan Phillips signing with the Braves. Another piece of news for the Brewers was about Jeferson Quero. The Brewers were officially granted a fourth option year for Quero , meaning they can keep him in the minors for one more year. Without the option, Quero would either have to make the roster out of spring training or potentially be exposed to waivers to keep in the minors. Now, the Brewers can give him one more season in Nashville to see what he can offer in the future. Early trade rumors are coming up for current Brewers’ players, mainly focused around the players who are free agents after the 2027 season. The main two players that have been mentioned in rumors so far are Trevor Megill and William Contreras. At the meetings, Matt Arnold spoke about the possibility of trading Contreras . He did it with usual GM speak, saying that Contreras “means a lot to this team”. When asked about Megill, he continued with the GM speak and said, “He got the last six outs of the World Series, and I just went to a Metallica concert with him, so I like him. I like him a lot.” The yearly awards were also announced at this year’s meetings, and as expected for the World Series champions, they were represented several times. Here is a summary of the awards that they won or received votes for: Logan Henderson finished sixth in the NL Rookie of the Year vote, with Sal Stewart of the Reds and Kevin McGonigle of the Tigers taking the award . sports.description: Canada embrace Concacaf experience in win over Guatemala By Ben Steiner A fireworks-filled anthem, a less-than-ideal playing surface, and cages surrounding the pitch. Away days in Concacaf aren’t for the faint of heart, but Canada scraped out a 3-2 win over Guatemala on Friday. Under head coach Jesse Marsch, Canada have faced some of the world's best teams and reached the FIFA World Cup Round of 16. Yet Friday's opening 45 minutes of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals may have been among their most complete, before a disheartening second half saw a 3-0 lead nearly disappear. Jonathan David brought his stellar LaLiga form to the Estadio El Trébol, posting 1g/1a and helping build up Canada’s third goal. Liam Millar, in dominant form in the EFL Championship, scored too, while former Minnesota United striker Tani Oluwaseyi netted his first for Canada in 18 appearances. “We were very happy with that start,” assistant coach Mauro Biello told reporters, taking media duties after Marsch’s second-half red card. “It was something that we addressed here in the build-up to be able to create more, to score more goals, and I think we're very happy with the way our forwards played. Especially in the first half, and getting goals from both strikers and Liam, who was also doing really well at his club.” Alphonso Davies blow It had been more than 600 days since Alphonso Davies last started for Canada, when he tore his ACL in the 2025 Nations League third-place game against the United States . It seemed as if his return, committing to playing for Les Rouges on a November night in Guatemala amid stellar FC Bayern Munich form, was him putting the last two years of injury troubles behind him. That hope lasted just five minutes before an awkward shot block sent him off the pitch early. sports.description: FBL-FRIENDLY-ARG-URU - AFP Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni has called for patience with his emerging youngsters after the Albiceleste suffered a 2-1 friendly defeat against Uruguay at La Bombonera on Friday. sports.title: Taking care of business among key Rangers takeaways in convincing win over Canucks
sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Plain and simple, the New York Rangers took care of business Friday night in Vancouver, overwhelming the last-place Canucks 5-1 at Rogers Arena. Which is exactly what should have been expected. Make no mistake, this is a game the Rangers (12-8-1) had to have. Not only to ensure a winning road trip in the Pacific Northwest, but because the Canucks (3-17-1) are an absolute train wreck, the worst team by far in the NHL. Though the Rangers started slowly in the first period, there was only one expected and acceptable outcome. And that was a Rangers victory. No excuses. Yes, the Canucks are that bad. They’ve now lost seven in a row, and have just one victory in their past 18 games (1-16-1) since Oct. 4 after winning two of their first three. They’re the worst defensive team in the League , allowing more than four and a half goals per game on average, and their penalty kill is simply atrocious. So, even though the Canucks took a 1-0 on an Elias Pettersson deflection at 12:13 of the first period, and the Rangers hadn’t won a game this season after giving up the first goal, there was no way visitors could lose this game. And they didn’t. Gabe Perreault ‘s short-side snipe at 18:47 of the first tied things up. And then it was a master class by the Rangers in the second period. They scored four unanswered goals in a span of 7:49, out-shot the Canucks 12-4, and had a whopping expected goal share 5v5 of 84.02 percent, per Natural Stat Trick . Through two periods, the Rangers had a 16-6 advantage in high-danger chances. They took their foot off the gas some in the third period, but Dylan Garand stopped all 13 shots he faced in the final frame. New York was the far better team at even strength, and on special teams — where they scored once on teh power play and were a perfect 3-for=3 on the penalty kill. Though none of this should come as a surprise. The Rangers took three of four on this road trip, after beginning it with just one road victory on the season. And this latest victory represented their first in nine games when allowing the first goal (1-7-1).4 They reach the season’s quarter-mark third in the Metropolitan Division, and winners in five of their past six games. technology.title: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed
technology.description: GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That's around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. Among GLP-1 users, nearly half (44 percent) reported using their GLP-1 in a way that was different from how it was prescribed. Users skipped doses, delayed getting refills, and used smaller doses than prescribed, among other changes. More than half of the people modifying how they used the drug said the changes were because of cost or availability reasons. Cost and access barriers were most pronounced among younger GLP-1 users.
